# Independent audit: positive cap-ceiling band for exact ordinary rows

Source: `candidate 5f923460093c970f`, all four sections. **PASS**. The band is proved positive but has no computed width; no implication for the specific ceiling `128/279` is established.

The affine/coarea normalization is correct: with contragredient normals, both areas and the coarea-normalized cutting sections acquire the same determinant factor. The raw ratios and row data are unchanged. Common normal rescaling is also harmless. Individual unit normalization is used only to obtain compact parameter sequences; its balance weights are retained and reconstructed before returning to row invariance.

A maximum-area inscribed triangle exists by compactness and has positive area. After mapping it to the reference triangle, replacing one vertex gives `|lambda_i(x)|<=1` for every body point. This supplies the stated fixed compact triangle enclosure. Support functions are uniformly bounded and Lipschitz; their limit contains the fixed reference triangle and retains the maximal-triangle area constraint by vertexwise approximation. Hence no dimension or area degeneracy occurs.

Moving-cap area convergence follows from dominated convergence outside the limiting body boundary and cutting lines, all of which have planar measure zero. The limiting source is initially allowed on the boundary. A vanishing balance weight would leave an opposite pair of limiting unit normals, whose captured fractions sum to one, contradicting `2 Gamma<1`. The same argument prevents a collinear positive circuit. Thus the limit has three positive weights and spans the plane.

The argument locating the limiting source is sound. A limiting cap containing the true centroid strictly has a positive-area strip beyond the parallel through-centroid cap, so its fraction exceeds `Gamma`. All scalar margins of centroid minus source are therefore nonpositive. Their positive weighted sum is zero, forcing every margin to vanish; spanning gives equality of source and centroid. All three limiting caps attain `Gamma`. The standard planar single-cap equality case makes the body a triangle, and the normalized maximal-area condition forces it to be exactly the reference triangle. Repeated equality directions would again produce an opposite pair, so the limiting incidence is strict and distinct.

The final matrix has the two reconstructed balanced normals as its rows. Its inverse transpose therefore sends them exactly to `e_1,e_2`, and sends the third to `-e_1-e_2`. This gives one fixed-normal problem with a convergent strict-incidence triangle limit. The independently audited full local-body theorem applies, including its strictness for nontriangles. This is the essential step that compactness and continuity alone cannot replace.

The alternative modulus conversion in Section 3 is also correct: the cap-cover profile gives `q_min>=Gamma-8 epsilon`, and its surplus is at most `9 epsilon/4`. The cited attained stability theorem uses a non-strict surplus premise, so the printed non-strict conversion is valid. The actual-fiber corollary uses only `q_i<=Q/k<=Gamma(1+a/k)` and does not silently replace the mixed body or its weights. Its sufficiently small uncomputed ratio is retained explicitly.

No repair required. Classical Grunbaum equality and the already audited local theorem are the only equality/rigidity inputs; no unknown minimizer classification or global OC statement is used.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
